evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only checks that both manager PIDs are positive and that PID and invocation ID both differ. A guest reboot between the two manager snapshots changes the manager PID and invocation ID, so the predicate can report an isolated manager restart even though the observations span a reboot. The snapshots already carry `boot_id` (used for the separate reboot checks), so the missing nonempty/equal boot-ID condition is a concrete false-positive bug in the existing check.
